newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian banker says privatise power, telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian banker says privatise power, telecoms.

text.p: The chief executive of the local unit of Ecobank, Disun Holloway, has told Nigeria's military government to privatise state-owned electricity and telecommunications companies to make them more efficient.

"The non-privatisation of the parastatals may continue to have a negative effect on the output and efficiency of the real sector of the economy," he said in a paper published in Thisday newspaper on the 1997 fiscal budget released last month.

His view tallies with those of many other experts who have commented on the budget, which had been expected to include a programme of privatisation but which instead said a committee would be set up to study the options open to the government.

"The budget appeared ambiguous on the anticipated privatisation or commercialisation of NITEL (Nigerian Telecommunications), NEPA (National Electric Power Authority) and other government parastatals," Holloway said.

Nigeria has since 1995 being trying to open up its economy through a policy of "guided deregulation" and last year senior government officials raised the prospect of selling off loss-making state enterprises including the vital oil industry.

Holloway praised the military government's management of the economy in 1996 especialy the successful stabilisation of the exchange rate of the naira currency, reduced interest rates and the downward spiral in inflation.
His bank operates in several West African cities and has its headquarters in Abidjan, Ivory Coast.
